source.title: Improving Generalization in Federated Learning by Seeking Flat Minima
source.authors: Debora Caldarola; Barbara Caputo; Marco Ciccone

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether flat-minima interventions improve federated models’ generalization and measures test accuracy and Hessian-based sharpness. It uses different models, settings, and measures from the claim versions’ specified studies.
record.gate_note: The study tests flat-minima and generalization relationships in federated learning. Rows below cover its CIFAR-10/100 accuracy and Hessian results, including the reported sharpness ratios. It also reports results on CIFAR100-PAM, Landmarks-User-160k, Cityscapes, IDDA, and corrupted CIFAR, which are not fully extracted here. Cited findings from prior work are not rows.
record.test_reason: Table 13 tests V4 in federated image classification: server-side SGD, Adam and AdaGrad are compared on held-out accuracy after learning-rate tuning. The Hessian and flat-minima experiments do not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap relationship.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they attribute degraded federated performance partly to sharp loss geometry and report that client-side SAM/ASAM and server-side SWA improve performance across several vision tasks. This is their interpretation, not a demonstrated magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap correlation; individual method combinations do not improve every setting.
record.recipe_differences: Federated training with client-side SAM/ASAM and server-side SWA, evaluated on natural vision data; the claim’s versions concern centralized memorization/generalization, size, architecture, optimizer, batch size, dropout, sharpness-gap measurement, and example removal.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with data heterogeneity, dataset, number of participating clients, choice of SAM versus ASAM, whether SWA is used, and SAM/ASAM/SWA hyperparameters. The authors report high SAM ρ can reduce performance; ASAM supports larger neighborhoods. SWA starting later in training improves its contribution.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM and ASAM generally reduce maximum Hessian eigenvalues; SWA's effects depend on the curvature statistic and partition. These measurements do not establish V7.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharpness-oriented optimization can alter Hessian curvature in federated CNNs.

fits_no_version.finding: With α=0 and five clients per round, FedASAM + SWA raises CIFAR-100 accuracy from 30.25% to 42.01% and CIFAR-10 accuracy from 65.00% to 76.44%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Client-side ASAM combined with server-side SWA can improve heterogeneous federated image-classification accuracy.

record.problems: The paper's sharpness evidence uses Hessian eigenvalues and loss-surface plots, not the magnitude-aware perturbation measure named in V7. The reported CIFAR tables give test accuracy but not paired training accuracy, so they do not quantify the train–test gap. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the extracted results.
record.rows_left_out: Rows for additional CIFAR10/100 alpha partitions and participating-client counts, CIFAR100-PAM, Landmarks-User-160k, Cityscapes, IDDA, corrupted CIFAR, and further optimizer/SWA ablations are not fully extracted. They appear in Tables 2–17 and Figures 6, 8–16; the reported findings are summarized in the paper’s Results sections and appendices. Prior-work findings cited in the paper were excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and corresponding natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Client-side adaptive versus SGD optimization, paired training performance, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching optimizers, and language benchmarks.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.

Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance correlated with train–test gaps among similarly fitted networks, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. Adaptive sharpness is an optimization objective here, not the evaluated generalization measure.
Removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

missing.what: Extract Table 13's server-optimizer comparisons for V4. Best tested SGD/Adam/AdaGrad accuracies are 30.25/29.75/26.25% at α=0 and 49.92/51.73/51.44% at α=1000. Preserve each optimizer's learning rate and distinguish the tuning sweep from the resulting comparison. Although optimizer ablations are broadly declared in rows_left_out, these results are necessary to capture the tested version.

record.verdict_notes: The decisive overlooked test is the server-side optimizer ablation. The accuracy datasets in R15–R18 are swapped, as confirmed by Tables 5, 6 and 17. No verdict on V7 follows from Hessian curvature or improved test accuracy alone.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization versus natural-label generalization is not tested.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold are not tested.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons are not tested.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD on held-out performance are not tested as a claim about optimizer generalization; server-side optimizer comparisons are included only as FL baselines.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets are not tested.

The paper tests whether Hessian eigenvalue measures and loss-surface geometry vary with test performance, but does not test magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness or rank it against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy is not tested.

rows.subject: FedAvg E=1
rows.size_stated: CNN similar to LeNet5; two 64-channel convolutional layers and fully connected layers of 384 and 192 channels
rows.operation_detail: Measured global model Hessian maximum eigenvalue and λmax/λ5 ratio after training.
rows.note: FedAvg is reported with E=1 in the table; associated prose describes the λmax as 93.5 in the most heterogeneous setting.
rows.check: Hessian eigenvalues do not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or its relationship with the train–test gap.

rows.subject: FedASAM

rows.operation_detail: Measured global model Hessian maximum eigenvalue and λmax/λ5 ratio after training with local ASAM.
rows.note: Authors report that ASAM leads to flatter minima; λmax decreases substantially, while the ratio is slightly lower than baseline.
rows.check: ASAM uses adaptive perturbations during optimization, but the reported measurement is Hessian curvature, not V7's measure or gap correlation.

rows.subject: FedAvg + SWA

rows.note: The authors state that although λmax is higher than without SWA, the lower ratio indicates the bulk of the spectrum lies in a lower-curvature region.
rows.check: The two curvature statistics cannot determine whether V7 holds; their disagreement is not partial evidence for V7.
